Waited 15s after DOMContentLoaded for Elfsight platform.js to bootstrap, then inspected the DOM for the overlay iframe and text signature. ALL 6 REQUESTED CHECKS PASS (6/6, 100%). Cross-origin Script error suppression works: no overlay iframe, no 'Uncaught runtime errors' text, no fixed high-z-index element, and NO uncaught page errors from our own code (the only 4 console errors are Elfsight's TikTok CORS fetches which are 3rd-party network noise, filename NOT empty, so unrelated to the fix). Reviews Elfsight widget (.elfsight-app-26818019-3adb-409f-a6d3-a8573ff17f0d) bootstraps correctly after scroll into view and renders 49 real Google reviews with 4.9 average rating (Jael Thalmann, Vanessa Jahn, elena v, A.G., Sarah Bernhard, …). Section header 'Was Schüler:innen sagen' + 5.0-Sterne-Google badge visible. Language toggle DE↔EN works (Hero: 'Fahrschule safe ride / Anders. Besser. Mutiger.' ↔ 'Learn to drive. / Different. Better. Bolder.'). Admin login works, edit mode toolbar visible at bottom-center (BEARBEITEN active, Live/VERWALTUNG/ANFRAGEN pill buttons), '⚡ Live-Widget einbetten' <details open> block shows the elfsight snippet in the multiline Editable, and 'Neu' button is correctly HIDDEN because embed is active. No changes required, fix is verified.
critical_code_review_comments: public/index.html top-of-<head> handler is correctly placed BEFORE any other script tag and uses capturing-phase (useCapture=true) with stopImmediatePropagation() – matches recommended pattern for suppressing browser-hidden CORS 'Script error.' events without swallowing genuine same-origin errors. The `!e.filename` guard is the correct signature.

The unhandledrejection handler only matches when reason.message includes 'Script error'. Some 3rd-party CDNs reject with non-Error objects or with the browser-generic 'Script error.'; consider also matching when reason is undefined/null or when the message is exactly '' – but this is defensive and not currently breaking anything.

ReviewsEmbedHtml + EmbedHtml (SocialFeed) both use `injectedHtmlRef` to skip re-injection when the same HTML string is seen twice. Good idempotency guard. Consider also debouncing rapid content updates via useMemo/hash, but not a bug.

The Elfsight widget makes cross-origin fetch to widget-data.service.elfsight.com/api/tiktok/profile which the browser blocks with CORS (visible as 4 console errors in ALL sessions). This is Elfsight-side and not user-visible. If it becomes noisy you could add a specific console.error filter but currently it is fine – the overlay does NOT appear from these because CORS fetch errors surface as network errors, not window.onerror.
The `assets.emergent.sh/scripts/emergent-main.js` <script src> in index.html (line 110) is loaded synchronously – consider `defer` to speed up first paint. Non-blocking issue.

rca of the issue: The webpack-dev-server's error overlay listens to window.onerror events. When Elfsight's platform.js (loaded from elfsightcdn.com) throws internal errors during its bootstrap or async data-fetch phase, the browser reports them as 'Script error.' with filename='' due to same-origin-policy protection (the response lacks CORS headers so browsers hide details). Webpack picks these up like any real runtime error and renders the red overlay. The fix installs a capturing-phase window.addEventListener('error', …) BEFORE bundle.js loads, filters events where message==='Script error.' AND !filename (the unmistakable CORS signature), and calls stopImmediatePropagation()+preventDefault() to prevent the webpack-dev-server client from ever seeing them. A twin handler for 'unhandledrejection' events with 'Script error' in the reason.message covers the promise-based bootstrap path. Additionally, ReviewsEmbedHtml + EmbedHtml components track the last-injected HTML in injectedHtmlRef; if the same HTML string is passed again (e.g., after a benign content re-render), the effect returns early — this prevents Elfsight's platform.js from being re-executed and complaining about double-init. Verified in this iteration: overlay does not appear, widget bootstraps, reviews render, no uncaught errors from our own code. Production builds don't include webpack-dev-server so this fix is purely dev/preview – no regression risk to production.
